items.title: Strong and concentrated are two different things
items.claim: A 0.0001 M solution of hydrochloric acid is a strong acid but dilute. A 12 M solution of ethanoic acid is concentrated but weak. Strength and concentration are independent properties.

options.text: Whether the acid fully dissociates into ions in water (strong) or only partially (weak); concentration is just how much acid is dissolved per unit volume
How much it costs to buy
Whether it is in a glass bottle

items.reveal:
Strong acids (HCl, HNO3, H2SO4, HBr, HI, HClO4) dissociate essentially 100 percent in water. The H+ concentration equals the acid concentration.

Weak acids (CH3COOH, HCN, H2CO3) only partially dissociate. Vinegar is about 1 M ethanoic acid but [H+] is only about 0.004 M — most of the acid stays as undissociated molecules.

Very dilute HCl is still a strong acid (fully dissociated) but has a low [H+]. Glacial ethanoic acid is highly concentrated but most molecules are intact. The pKa describes strength; molarity describes concentration. Confusing them is a common GCSE error.
items.why: Strength and concentration are routinely conflated. They measure entirely different physical properties of an acid.

items.title: pH 1 to pH 2 is a tenfold change, not a small one
items.claim: The pH scale runs from 0 to 14 and looks linear. It isn't. pH is the negative logarithm of [H+]. Each step on the scale is a factor of 10 in hydrogen-ion concentration.
items.prompt: How much more acidic is stomach acid (pH 1) than pure water (pH 7)?
items.reveal:
pH = -log10[H+]. Stomach acid at pH 1 has [H+] = 0.1 M. Pure water at pH 7 has [H+] = 10 to the minus 7 M. The ratio is 10 to the 6 — a million.

This is why diluting a strong acid even tenfold barely changes its pH: the absolute concentration drops by a factor of 10, the pH only shifts by 1 unit.

The same logic applies to the Richter scale (earthquakes), decibels (sound intensity), and stellar magnitudes (brightness). Logarithmic scales let humans handle quantities spanning many orders of magnitude — but they hide the underlying spread.
items.why: Linear-looking scales can describe quantities ranging over 14 orders of magnitude. Acidity's arithmetic must respect the log.
